findings.summary: The help center ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode capture is pixel-equivalent to the light capture; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and the same light rgb(240, 242, 245) body background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, border and icon colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Mobile browsers receive a desktop 980 CSS-pixel layout scaled down to 360 device pixels.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 device viewport, layout reports hasViewportMeta:false, innerWidth:980 and scale:0.367. Screenshots show the permanent desktop sidebar and very small content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard width=device-width, initial-scale=1 viewport declaration, then reflow to a single-column layout and collapse the sidebar into an accessible navigation drawer.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation chrome consumes a disproportionate share of the small-screen layout.
findings.evidence: On article and category mobile captures, the always-visible left navigation occupies about 110 of 360 physical pixels before the content column.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact header and dismissible, focus-managed navigation drawer below the mobile breakpoint so article content gets the viewport.

findings.summary: The rendered accessibility structure contains malformed ARIA/list relationships.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports aria-required-children, list and listitem failures, and an agent accessibility-tree failure. The DOM also exposes core navigation controls as DIV role=button.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace simulated controls with native buttons and repair list ownership so every list has only valid li children and required ARIA descendants.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is programmatically reachable but has no visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused the Help Center link, language control, all sidebar buttons, search input and article links; every sampled element reported outline:none and boxShadow:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator with sufficient offset for every interactive control and verify a complete keyboard focus walk.

findings.summary: Cold-load paint performance is far outside the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured FCP 13.2s and LCP 17.5s (performance 0.55). A separate trace measured FCP/LCP 2.25s, showing network variability but corroborating that the page is delivery-bound rather than main-thread-bound.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP discovery and prioritize only the critical content path; remove noncritical page shell code and defer below-the-fold work.

findings.summary: The page ships a long critical delivery chain and multi-megabyte payload for a simple help index.
findings.evidence: HAR records 41 requests and 3,150,112 transferred bytes, including two VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets. Lighthouse reports render-blocking savings of 1.35s and a 3,063 KiB payload.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline or isolate minimal critical CSS, split route-specific assets, preload only the actual LCP resource, and defer noncritical styles/scripts.

findings.summary: Most shipped CSS and JavaScript is unused on the help-center homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,906 KiB unused JavaScript and 306 KiB unused CSS; many individual bundles are over 90% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a help-center-specific entry point, split by route/feature, and conditionally load search, feedback, and article-only code.

findings.summary: Text is physically too small to read comfortably on mobile.
findings.evidence: The page computes 12px body text inside a 980px layout that Chrome scales to 0.367, producing roughly 4.4 physical-pixel text in the mobile captures.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix viewport/reflow first, then use readable rem-based type and line-height with fluid scaling and a comfortable article measure.

findings.summary: The missing viewport declaration defeats mobile reflow and makes apparent target sizes misleading.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive reports hasViewportMeta:false and Chrome emulates a 980px layout scaled down. Lighthouse separately fails meta-viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a zoom-permissive viewport declaration and retest at 320 CSS px, 200% zoom, touch and keyboard conditions.

findings.summary: Document encoding and image sizing hygiene are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a missing/late charset. The article image audit finds all 16 images missing at least one explicit dimension, 15 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and one missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare UTF-8 in the first 1024 bytes, set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, lazy-load below-fold images, and supply meaningful or empty alt text.

findings.summary: The page uses deprecated APIs and is not eligible for back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecated-API warning and four BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the Lighthouse audit details, replace the deprecated API, and remove avoidable unload/state blockers so article back-navigation restores instantly.

findings.summary: Article pages lack a page-specific meta description.
findings.evidence: The sampled article has a descriptive title but article-probe reports description:null.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render a concise, unique meta description derived from each article summary.

findings.summary: Crawler and mobile indexing signals are broken or incomplete.
findings.evidence: robots.txt and sitemap.xml redirect to the generic error route; Lighthouse reports robots.txt invalid with 73 errors, and the page has no viewport meta.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve valid text/plain robots.txt and an XML sitemap with 200 responses, and add the standard viewport declaration.

findings.summary: Help articles expose no structured data or social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The article metadata probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Article/TechArticle JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching the visible title, summary, canonical URL and media.

findings.summary: The otherwise strong security-header set omits Referrer-Policy and allows inline styles.
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY and a nonce-based script policy, but Referrer-Policy is missing and style-src contains unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a deliberate Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin and migrate inline styles toward nonces/hashes or constrained style sources.

findings.summary: Core help content disappears when JavaScript is unavailable.
findings.evidence: Discoverability reports isJsShell:true with only 6% raw/rendered word coverage on home and 3% on the article; crawler screenshots are blank while rendered screenshots contain the content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render article/index content and real links, then hydrate search, navigation and feedback as enhancements.

findings.summary: Article imagery is routinely oversized and eagerly loaded.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 8 of 16 images over 2x display width, 15 below-fold images without lazy loading and one legacy PNG.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized responsive sources, retain modern formats, set intrinsic dimensions and lazy-load below-fold instructional images.

findings.summary: The resource footprint is disproportionate to a mostly text-and-links help page.
findings.evidence: The 3.15 MB load is 2.52 MB JavaScript; Lighthouse estimates about 1.9 MB of that JavaScript and 306 KiB CSS are unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Budget the help shell independently, remove shared product code, and load route capabilities only when requested.

findings.summary: The initial heap footprint is large for a static help index.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 1,048,981 nodes and 55,025,709 bytes self size; after ten representative navigation toggles the fresh-run snapshot is 56,444,423 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the shared client runtime and DOM/state graph; profile retained objects after route-specific code splitting.
